q: Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land.

s: Jacob's vow has condition God's presence, protection, provision, and safe return (if God will be with him)
q: If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,

s: Jacob's vow promises tenth (tithe) (of all God gives him)
q: Of all that you will give me I will surely give a tenth to you.

s: Jacob's vow promises stone pillar (Jacob's stone at Bethel) (will be God's house)
q: then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, will be God’s house.

s: Jacob departed from Beersheba
q: Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.

s: Jacob sibling of Esau
q: Jacob’s and Esau’s mother

s: Jacob has grandfather Bethuel (maternal grandfather)
q: the house of Bethuel your mother’s father

s: Jacob has uncle Laban (mother's brother)
q: the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.

s: Jacob obeys Isaac (obeyed father and mother)
q: Jacob obeyed his father and his mother

s: Isaac forbids marriage to daughters of Canaan (command to Jacob)
q: You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

s: Isaac is displeased by daughters of Canaan
q: the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.

s: Laban is son of Nahor
q: Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?

s: Jacob is husband of Rachel (married after serving seven more years)
q: He gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.

s: Jacob is husband of Leah (given in place of Rachel)
q: In the evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to Jacob. He went in to her.

s: Leah has servant Zilpah (given by Laban)
q: Laban gave Zilpah his servant to his daughter Leah for a servant.

s: Rachel has servant Bilhah (given by Laban)
q: Laban gave Bilhah, his servant, to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.

s: Rachel is barren
q: but Rachel was barren.

s: Leah is hated (as seen by the LORD; less loved than Rachel)
q: The LORD saw that Leah was hated

s: Jacob loves more Rachel (more than Leah)
q: he loved also Rachel more than Leah

s: Leah is mother of Reuben
q: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben.

s: Leah is mother of Simeon
q: She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.

s: Leah is mother of Levi
q: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.

s: Rachel is daughter of Laban
q: See, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.

s: Leah is mother of Judah
q: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah.

s: LORD opened Leah (opened her womb)
q: he opened her womb

s: well (in the field where Jacob met Rachel) has feature large stone on its mouth
q: The stone on the well’s mouth was large.

s: well (in the field where Jacob met Rachel) is located in land of the children of the east (in a field)
q: Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.

s: well (in the field where Jacob met Rachel) is used for watering flocks
q: For out of that well they watered the flocks.

s: seven years of service (Jacob for Rachel) has duration seven years (Jacob's service to Laban for Rachel)
q: Jacob served seven years for Rachel.

s: Laban says to jacob Surely you are my bone and my flesh
q: Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.”

s: Laban is brother of Rebekah (Laban is Jacob's mother's brother)
q: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother

s: Jacob is son of Rebekah
q: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s relative, and that he was Rebekah’s son.
